headline: Shifting Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill aims to reduce residential electricity bills by requiring large energy users, such as data centers, to bear more of the costs for grid infrastructure and capacity.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, Dominion Energy (with amendments)
opponents: Data center industry, large manufacturers, industry lobbying groups
news_headline: Virginia bill aims to cut residential energy costs
news_summary: A bill in Virginia seeks to shift energy costs to data centers and other large users, potentially saving residential customers over $65 annually. Governor Spanberger signed legislation that directs regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers and allows Dominion Energy to spend more on burying distribution lines, though some amendments were made.

headline: Mandatory Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water providers to report the monthly water consumption of data centers to the State Water Control Board, including reclaimed water, to increase transparency.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates, Potomac Conservancy
opponents: Data center industry (due to increased reporting burden/scrutiny)
news_headline: Data centers are drinking our Potomac River region resources
news_summary: The Potomac Conservancy is advocating for SB 553, a bill that would require data centers to report their water usage to the State Water Control Board, citing concerns about water supply in the Potomac River region. This transparency is crucial for understanding and addressing the impact of data center sprawl on Virginia's natural resources.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Regulations
short_summary: This bill mandates that local governments require site assessments for large data centers, including noise and environmental impacts, to protect nearby communities and align with local planning.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residential groups, environmental groups, historic preservation advocates, farmland protection groups
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce, pro-growth business groups
news_headline: As data center noise concerns grow, Loudoun Co. officials discuss possible mitigation efforts
news_summary: Residents in Loudoun County are experiencing significant noise pollution from data centers, leading officials to discuss mitigation efforts and potential changes to zoning and noise ordinances. HB 153 requires site assessments for large data centers, including noise and environmental impacts, to help localities make informed decisions and protect communities.
